discovery: Discovery of baryon acoustic oscillations in the large-scale distribution of galaxies

nominees.name: Daniel J. Eisenstein
nominees.affiliation: Harvard University (Center for Astrophysics | Harvard & Smithsonian), USA

nominees.name: Will J. Percival
nominees.affiliation: University of Waterloo and Perimeter Institute, Canada

motivation: In 2005 the Sloan Digital Sky Survey (Eisenstein et al.) and the 2dF Galaxy Redshift Survey (Cole, Percival et al.) independently detected the baryon acoustic oscillation feature, a fossil sound wave from the primordial photon-baryon plasma, imprinted on the clustering of galaxies. Eisenstein supplied the theoretical framework that made the feature a usable standard ruler. The detection showed that the structure seen in the CMB grew under gravity into today's cosmic web. It confirmed that baryons are a minority component within a dominant cold dark matter, and it gave cosmology a robust geometric probe of the expansion history. BAO is now the backbone of BOSS, eBOSS, DESI and Euclid. DESI's 2024-25 results, which hint at evolving dark energy, show that this ruler still drives fundamental physics. The discovery changed how we measure the contents of the Universe.
